candidate_rule: Each record yields two non-promoted candidates: its verified fact and the explicit source scope guard.

scope_guards.cn_spring26: National coverage, take-up and prediction figures are aggregate snapshots, not live exact-address orderability or performance evidence.
scope_guards.pnd26: All deployment figures are conditional operator plans and must not be treated as completed builds or current parcel truth.
scope_guards.bduk_june26: Rounded monthly contract management information has ingestion lag and revisions; it does not identify delivered UPRNs or current retail service.
scope_guards.complaints_q1_26: Complaint trends and provider rankings are aggregate regulator evidence, not address-level reliability or coverage facts.
scope_guards.map_mobile_1m: Postcode, postal-district, crowdsourced and predicted checker data cannot guarantee indoor signal, capacity or exact-property performance.

records: The Spring 2026 Connected Nations update is a snapshot of UK mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises as of January 2026.
Full-fibre availability represented 82% of UK homes.
The residential premise base used for the full-fibre figure was 30.5 million UK homes.
An additional 1.2 million homes gained potential access to full fibre in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre connection take-up across residential and commercial premises increased by 1.8 million in six months.
Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million connections across all UK premises.
Full-fibre take-up corresponded to 47% of premises with access to full fibre.
Gigabit-capable broadband was available to 27.1 million UK homes.
Gigabit-capable availability reached 89% of UK homes.
Gigabit-capable availability had been 26.4 million homes, or 87%, in July 2025.
Only 4,000 premises were reported without access to affordable decent broadband, mainly after lower-priced satellite services became available.
Premises unable to access decent broadband from fixed-line or fixed wireless networks fell to 39,000 from 44,000 in July 2025.
Predicted good 4G geographic coverage from all mobile network operators reached 84% of UK landmass, a three-percentage-point increase.
Predicted good 4G geographic coverage from at least one mobile network operator remained at 96% of UK landmass.
Each mobile network operator maintained predicted coverage of at least 99% outside UK premises.
High-confidence 5G standalone coverage outside premises ranged from 49% to 85% across the three operators that had deployed it, compared with 47% to 65% in July 2025.
Overall 5G coverage outside premises ranged from 76% to 94% by operator, while coverage from all operators increased from 47% to 64%.
The 2026 planned-deployment report is based on network operators' stated plans as of January 2026 for the following three years.
The plan set includes privately funded and publicly supported operator deployments but excludes separate rollout aspirations of public authorities.
If all stated plans are realised, full fibre could reach 28.1 million UK homes by January 2029.
The 28.1 million-home full-fibre forecast represents 92% of residential properties.
The forecast starts from 24.9 million homes, or 82%, with full-fibre access in January 2026.
Gigabit-capable coverage could reach 29 million homes by January 2029 if all plans are delivered.
The January 2029 gigabit-capable forecast represents 95% of UK homes.
The gigabit-capable baseline was 27.1 million homes, or 89%, in January 2026.
Full-fibre coverage under all plans was projected at 90% by January 2028, down from a 95% projection in the previous year's report.
High-confidence plans implied 87% full-fibre coverage by January 2028, compared with 86% from the previous year's plans.
High-confidence plans implied 88% full-fibre coverage by January 2029.
Northern Ireland's full-fibre projection under all plans remained at 99% by January 2029.
Urban gigabit-capable coverage could increase from 24.2 million homes (93%) in January 2026 to 25.3 million (97%) by January 2029.
Rural gigabit-capable coverage could increase from 2.9 million homes (66%) to 3.7 million (86%) by January 2029.
If all plans are realised, 95% of local authorities were estimated to reach at least 85% gigabit-capable residential coverage by January 2029.
By the end of 2028, 73% of UK homes, or 22.2 million, were forecast to have access to at least two gigabit-capable networks.
By the end of 2028, 36% of UK homes, or 11.1 million, were forecast to have access to at least three gigabit-capable networks.
Around 6,950 geographically distinct fixed-wireless masts were planned or due for upgrade to support at least 100 Mbit/s services between January 2026 and January 2029.

In Q1 2026, overall complaints decreased quarter on quarter; fixed-broadband and pay-monthly-mobile complaints decreased, while landline and pay-TV complaints were unchanged.
Plusnet and TalkTalk generated the most landline complaints, and both increased relative to the previous quarter.
EE, Sky, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Vodafone generated the fewest landline complaints.
Sky Mobile was the most complained-about pay-monthly mobile provider, with complaints primarily driven by experiences changing provider.
EE, Giffgaff, Tesco Mobile, Three and Vodafone generated the fewest pay-monthly mobile complaints.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used its free Map Your Mobile checker by 29 May 2026.
The checker accepts a postcode and presents network availability maps plus a performance score for the postal district.
Map Your Mobile combines crowdsourced Opensignal experience data with predictive information from mobile network operators and is regularly refreshed.
